_comment: Phase 2 ratchet baseline for issue #691 (RHI: Vulkan backend alongside OpenGL 4.6).
THESE NUMBERS MAY ONLY EVER GO DOWN. RHIBoundaryRatchetTest fails if any
counter rises above its baseline. When you lower one, edit the number here in
the same commit — the test prints the exact value to paste.
Do NOT raise a baseline to make the build green. A rise means new raw OpenGL
was added outside Platform/OpenGL/, which is the regression the ratchet
exists to catch. Route it through the RendererAPI facade instead; if that
genuinely cannot express it, that is a Phase 2 design gap worth a comment on
#691, not a baseline bump.
Counting rule (implemented in RHIBoundaryRatchetTest.cpp, must match this):
an identifier matching gl[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]* immediately followed by '(',
counted AFTER C/C++ comments and string/char literal bodies are stripped.
Stripping matters less than pattern precision: with the same pattern it
removes only 16 of 565 hits, whereas a pattern loose enough to match glfw*
is what produced the task handover's '724' (the issue body's '~620' was a
rough estimate). Both are done here so the number a test asserts on is exact.
Buckets and what they mean — see ADR 0011 sections 0, 1.6 and 1.7:
sweep  = OloEngine/src/** minus Platform/OpenGL/ minus Renderer/Debug/.
Phase 2 target. MUST reach zero.
tools  = OloEngine/src/OloEngine/Renderer/Debug/. Phase 8 target. These
are RELOCATED behind a neutral interface into Platform/OpenGL/,
not exempted: CLAUDE.md's rendering-verification rule is enforced
through these tools and the MCP capture endpoints they back, so a
Vulkan backend they cannot see is one Phase 7 cannot verify.
Platform/OpenGL/ is the backend and is not counted at all.
sweep_glad_includes is the counter that actually PROVES the property: a
translation unit that cannot see <glad/gl.h> provably cannot name a GL
symbol, whereas a call count can be gamed by a helper that still lives in
Renderer/. It is not yet meaningful, though, because RendererAPI.h itself
includes <glad/gl.h> and every pass includes RendererAPI.h — so the symbols
arrive transitively and removing a per-file include changes nothing. Strip
the GLenum/GLuint parameters out of RendererAPI's virtuals FIRST (ADR 0011
section 1.7); only then does each removed include become a real guarantee.
debug_escape_hatch is uses of RHI::GetNativeHandleForDebug outside
Renderer/Debug/ and Platform/. It starts at zero and must stay there: the
whole point of that spelling is that it is conspicuous in review.
PHASE 2 STEP 1 (2026-07-30): sweep_glad_includes 70 -> 39. RendererAPI's
GLenum/GLuint/GLint virtuals are gone, so RendererAPI.h no longer includes
<glad/gl.h> and neither do the two RenderCommand facades — which makes every
per-file include removal a real, compiler-enforced guarantee for the first
time (ADR 0011 section 1.7's ordering constraint, now satisfied).
sweep_gl_calls deliberately did NOT move: step 1 converts the facade's
vocabulary, step 2 sweeps the raw call sites. A drop here would have meant
calls were hidden rather than removed.
The 39 is 34 removals against 3 ADDITIONS, and the additions are correct:
Renderer3DLifecycle.cpp, UIRenderer.cpp and Scene.cpp call GL but had no
direct include, relying on RendererAPI.h's transitive one (ADR 0011 section 0
predicted exactly 3 such files). Closing that path makes them name their own
dependency. Do NOT 'fix' that bump by re-hiding them behind a transitive
include — they are step-2 sweep backlog, and the counter is now honest.
Two transitive sources were found, not one. The second was wider and is the
reason this counter could have read zero while proving nothing:
Debug/Instrumentor.h included <tracy/TracyOpenGL.hpp>, and Instrumentor.h is
in OloEnginePCH.h — so every TU in the engine saw the whole GL API. The
OLO_PROFILE_GPU* macros it served were used nowhere, so the include was
deleted. A per-file #include scan cannot see a PCH; check it by hand.
PHASE 2 STEP 2 (2026-07-30): sweep_gl_calls 313 -> 0 and
sweep_glad_includes 39 -> 0. The sweep bucket now contains no raw OpenGL
call and no translation unit in it can name a GL symbol at all. Phase 2's
headline target is met.
BOTH ZEROES ARE NOW FLOORS, NOT TARGETS. A rise in either is a real
regression with no remaining excuse: the facade gained ~60 virtuals in this
step precisely so every operation the engine performs has a neutral
spelling (buffer binding points, buffer/framebuffer/VAO/query/fence
lifecycle, named-framebuffer draw+read attachment selection, blits, texture
clear/upload/readback, debug markers, device idle, MSAA caps). If you find
an operation with no facade entry point, add the virtual — do not reach for
glad.
Three things this step is worth remembering for:
1. The counter reaching zero was NOT the end of the work. A Platform/OpenGL
header included from the sweep bucket leaks the whole GL API just as
effectively as <glad/gl.h>, and this scan cannot see it. Three passes
(FluidIntermediatesPass, WaterRenderPass, VirtualMeshRegistry) included
Platform/OpenGL/OpenGLUtilities.h for GLClearProgramGuard. The fix was to
move the guard INTO the backend clear implementations where it belongs —
not to delete the glad include and call it done, which would have zeroed
this counter while proving nothing. Check for Platform/<Backend>/ includes
by hand, exactly like the PCH.
2. Zero GL CALLS does not mean zero GL. UIRenderer.cpp had no calls but typed
its clip-rect stack in GLint/GLsizei, so it genuinely could not compile
without the header. Removing an include is only safe when the file names
no GL* identifier of any kind — and only a compile proves it.
3. A loader-symbol probe is invisible here by construction. RGCommandContext
guarded its debug markers with `if (GLAD_GL_KHR_debug)`, which does not
match gl[A-Z] and so never appeared in this count. The capability check
moved into OpenGLRendererAPI::PushDebugGroup. Same class as step 1's
`glad_glCreateTextures != nullptr` context probe.
PHASE 2 STEP 3, PART 1 (2026-07-31): the identity currency gets a MINT, and
three counters to sweep onto it. Steps 1 and 2 removed GL's vocabulary and
GL's calls; step 3 removes GL's CURRENCY — the u32 `GetRendererID()` that ADR
0011 section 1.1 identifies as one integer conflating object identity, driver
handle and binding address.
WHAT LANDED: Renderer/RHI/RHIResourceRegistry — the generation-checked
producer of RHI::ResourceHandle, with contract tests. Phase 1 declared the
handle and specified what it means; nothing minted one, and
GetNativeHandleForDebug was declared and defined nowhere. Both are now real.
WHAT DID NOT LAND: the call-site conversion onto it. THE COUNTERS BELOW ARE
THEREFORE NOT ZERO, and that is deliberate and honest — they measure the work
remaining, exactly as sweep_gl_calls started at 313 and sweep_glad_includes
at 70. This mirrors how Phase 1 shipped: a vocabulary plus a ratchet, nothing
converted yet.
Three new counters, all monotonically non-increasing, all targeting zero:
WHICH COUNTER MEANS WHAT — corrected once the first real migration exposed it:
sweep_renderer_id UNDERCOUNTS. It measures the ACCESSOR NAME, not the
currency. A pass holding `u32 m_NoiseTexture` from CreateTexture2D contains
no `RendererID` token at all and is nonetheless entirely unmigrated —
SSAORenderPass has 2 RendererID mentions against 5 native texture ids.
Driving it to zero proves 'nobody calls GetRendererID', NOT 'no native ids
flow through the engine'.
facade_native_id_params IS THE COMPLETION CRITERION. When the u32 facade
forms are deleted, no caller CAN hold a native id — the type system enforces
it, which is the same 'provable rather than measured' property section 1.7
credits sweep_glad_includes with. Treat sweep_renderer_id as a progress
proxy and facade_native_id_params as the proof.
sweep_renderer_id      = mentions of the identifier `RendererID` in any
spelling (GetRendererID, the `using RendererID =
u32` alias, the backend's m_RendererID member)
outside Platform/ and Renderer/Debug/. A native
object name may not be NAMED there, let alone held.
699 across 79 files; the heaviest are
Renderer3DMeshSubmission.cpp (70),
Commands/RenderCommand.h (68),
Commands/CommandDispatch.cpp (67), Scene.cpp (65).
facade_native_id_params= parameters in RendererAPI.h declared `u32 <name>ID`.
This one goes to zero LAST, not first, and the
reason is an asymmetry worth internalising:
handle -> native is a registry lookup, but
native -> handle is NOT RECOVERABLE (a driver name
does not identify a slot). So a facade that takes
handles cannot serve a caller still holding a u32,
whereas a facade offering BOTH can serve either.
Order is therefore: add handle overloads (backends
resolve internally), migrate callers subsystem by
subsystem, then delete the u32 forms — at which
point this counter drops to zero in one step and
the boundary becomes compiler-enforced.
(An earlier note here said 'drive it to zero
FIRST'. That was reasoned from an all-at-once
conversion, where flipping the facade forces every
call site at once — which is exactly the
unreviewable change this plan avoids.)
backend_resolve_hatch  = uses of ResourceRegistry::ResolveNativeForBackend
outside Platform/. Sibling of debug_escape_hatch:
two conspicuously-named hatches out of a handle,
each baselined at zero where it does not belong.
Renderer/RHI/ is excluded because it declares and
defines the function. Starts at zero and must stay
there — the sweep must not smuggle native names out.
THE COUNTERS ARE A PROGRESS MEASURE, NOT THE PROOF, and it is worth being
precise about why. A count of `RendererID` mentions is gameable — rename the
accessor and it reads zero while a native GL name still crosses the boundary.
What is NOT gameable is the type system: there is no implicit conversion
between RHI::ResourceHandle and an integer in either direction, so once the
facade takes handles, a translation unit holding a native name cannot call
it. (Handle is an aggregate, so C++20 parenthesized aggregate init makes the
EXPLICIT spelling ResourceHandle(someId) well-formed — a narrow, conspicuous
hole that is self-defusing because the result carries Generation == 0 and so
fails IsValid() and resolves to 0. Both facts are asserted in
ResourceHandleCannotBeSpelledAsANativeId, which found this by asserting the
opposite and failing to compile.)
That is the same 'provable rather than measured' property section 1.7 credits
sweep_glad_includes with, one level up. ResourceHandleCannotBeSpelledAsANativeId
static_asserts the non-convertibility both ways, so a well-meant `Handle(u32)`
convenience constructor cannot silently reopen the boundary before the sweep
even starts.
TWO TRAPS FOUND BY AN ABANDONED FULL-SWEEP ATTEMPT, recorded because they cost
real time and neither is obvious (the full account, including three
scripted-edit defect classes, is in
docs/agent-rules/rhi-abstraction-boundary.md section 4):
1. A `.data()` boundary is where the type system stops helping. CreateQueries
passes `std::span<u32>::data()` to glCreateQueries; re-typing that span to
std::span<RHI::ResourceHandle> KEEPS COMPILING and has GL write 4-byte names
over an array of 8-byte handles. Grep for .data() on any container whose
element type changes.
2. Every Delete* virtual needs TWO changes, and only one is obvious: resolve
the handle to call glDelete*, AND unregister it. Skip the second and the
slot keeps its generation, so a handle to a destroyed object goes on
resolving to a name the driver may reissue — the recycled-name failure the
whole layer exists to prevent, reintroduced at the site most likely to be
treated as mechanical.
PHASE 2 STEP 3, SLICE 5 (2026-08-01): the framebuffer ATTACHMENT consumers.
sweep_renderer_id 699 -> 653. facade_native_id_params deliberately UNCHANGED
at 68: this slice adds handle overloads and deletes no u32 form, which is the
documented order (add overloads, migrate callers, delete the u32 forms last).
Migrated: all seven bakers, the straightforward bind passes (Fog, Overdraw,
SelectionOutline, Cloudscape composite, Decal, Bloom), every attachment read
in DDGIProbeUpdatePass, and RenderGraph's attachment clear + NaN census.
Eight sites were deliberately left native; the reason for each is tabulated in
docs/agent-rules/rhi-abstraction-boundary.md ('What slice 5 actually moved').
SIX NEW FACADE VIRTUALS were needed, against a worklist that predicted zero:
CopyImageSubData, CopyImageSubDataFull, ClearTextureFloat, the offset form of
UploadTextureSubImage2D, ReadTextureImage, ReadTextureSubImage. The prediction
was wrong because the survey behind it counted only BIND sinks, and the
attachment getters also feed a copy family (bakers staging an attachment into a
persistent texture) and a readback family (thumbnail / probe capture). Same
lesson as the SetTextureFilter/SetTextureWrap/UploadTextureSubImage2D discovery
one slice earlier: migrate one real consumer PER SINK FAMILY and let the
compiler enumerate the rest.
TWO SILENT DEFECTS FOUND, both worth knowing beyond this issue:
1. Hashing a driver name into a cache fingerprint cannot see a
destroy-then-recreate. RenderPipeline hashed DDGI's atlas ids so a
Resolution/HitCacheTexels edit would rebuild the frame graph — but
EnsureResources calls DestroyResources() BEFORE creating the replacements,
so GL may reissue the same names and the fingerprint never changed. The
graph then kept an import whose Width/Height described the OLD resolution.
Now hashes RHI::HashKey(handle); pinned by RHIResourceRegistry's
HashKeyDiffersAcrossADestroyRecreateThatReusesTheNativeName. Note the
opposite teardown order (allocate-then-release) hides this completely, so
whether the bug is live depends on a line nowhere near the hash.
2. ImportTextureHandle BLINDS RenderGraph::ResolveTexture, and that is what the
MCP capture endpoints read. textureID and identity are alternatives on a
PhysicalTexture, so a handle-imported resource resolves natively to 0 —
olo_render_list_targets reports id 0 and olo_render_capture_target cannot
find it. #732 already did this to SSAO's noise texture. Fixed with a
fallback through RHI::GetNativeHandleForDebug in OloEditor (which this
scanner does not walk, so debug_escape_hatch stays honestly 0 rather than
being waived). CONSEQUENCE FOR LATER SLICES: a resource's import may only
move to ImportTextureHandle after the diagnostics can read one — which is
why DDGI's importAtlas is still native here.
PHASE 2 STEP 3, SLICE 6 (2026-08-01): the command-layer bind cache — the
CURRENCY itself, not one producer family. sweep_renderer_id 653 -> 355 (six
times slice 5's move); facade_native_id_params 68 -> 67.
`using RendererID = u32` is DELETED. Every GPU-object field on the POD
command structs, the redundant-bind cache (BoundTextures / BoundUBOs /
CurrentBoundShader / CurrentBoundVAO / the six per-frame shadow fields),
DepthPrepassShaderIDs, InstanceGroupKey and the draw sort keys are
RHI::ResourceHandle now.
THREE CORRECTNESS FIXES, not just a type change:
1. InstanceGroupKey batched draws by VAO GL NAME. A delete/create pair can
hand two objects the same name, merging unrelated draws into one batch —
one mesh rendered with another's geometry. Two live handles cannot
collide.
2. DepthPrepassShaderIDs compared PROGRAMS by GL name to decide whether a
material's shader could be swapped for the depth-only one. A relinked
program can inherit a freed name across a hot reload.
3. RenderPipeline's shadow and IBL fingerprints hashed raw ids. ShadowMap
::SetSettings calls Shutdown() BEFORE Init() on a resolution change, so
GL may reissue the freed names and the hash would see no change — the
same defect the DDGI atlases had in slice 5.
THE DOC CLAIM THIS SLICE FALSIFIED. rhi-abstraction-boundary.md said keying
the cache on identities makes the Invalidate* calls 'a pure optimisation'.
That is WRONG and wrong in the direction that ships bugs. The recycled-name
collision does die — but an IN-PLACE RELOAD deliberately PRESERVES the
identity while replacing the storage (ScopedResourceHandle::Sync never
retires; that is what makes caching a handle safe). The cache then holds the
very handle being rebound, concludes 'already bound', and SKIPS a bind that
must happen — leaving the unit pointing at a deleted GL name. Under native-id
keying that self-corrected because the name changed. So every site that
recreates a texture's storage MUST call InvalidateTextureBinding. The doc is
corrected in this commit.
WHEN A MIGRATION SEEMS TO REQUIRE RAISING A RATCHET, THE CALL SITE IS USUALLY
WRONG. DrawElementsIndirectRaw(vaoID, bufferID) needed a handle form, and the
obvious mixed (handle, u32 bufferID) overload would have pushed
facade_native_id_params to 69. Its ONE caller had already run BindVAOIfNeeded,
so the draw was re-binding the VAO behind the redundant-bind cache's back;
DrawBoundElementsIndirect(u32) replaced both u32 forms, removed the redundant
bind, and netted -1 instead of +2.
PHASE 2 STEP 3, SLICE 7 (2026-08-01): item 3's leftovers. 355 -> 347.
All eight sites deferred by slice 5 as 'blocked on the transient pool' are
migrated. THE BLOCKER WAS NEVER REAL, and how it got recorded as fact is the
part worth keeping: TransientPool::AcquireTexture returns a Ref<Texture2D>,
which has minted handles since slice 2. AcquiredInfo::RendererID is a
diagnostics field with no role in resolution. What actually stood in the way
was PhysicalTexture's documented invariant that TextureID and Handle are
'ALTERNATIVES, exactly one is set' -- correct for an IMPORT (an importer only
has one currency, and neither is derivable from the other), never true for a
TRANSIENT (the planner holds the pooled Ref, so it has both and reads them
off one pointer in one statement).
So: when a migration says 'blocked on X', check whether X is a missing
CAPABILITY or an INVARIANT someone wrote down. The first is work; the second
is a decision that can be revisited once you know which case it was written
for. Not checking cost a slice of imagined work and put a false claim on the
issue tracker until it was corrected.
Bonus: each of those sites guards its copy with `if (src != dst)`. Those now
compare OBJECTS, so a recycled driver name can no longer make a source and
its export look identical and skip a copy the frame needed -- the
InstanceGroupKey defect class, in four more places.
REVIEW PASS (2026-08-01): 347 -> 345, and the split is a live demonstration
of the UNDERCOUNT warning above. Two fixes landed: Texture::operator== moved
off GetRendererID (-2, the whole delta), and three sort keys in
Renderer3DSpecializedDraws.cpp moved from cmd->shader->GetRendererID() to
cmd->shaderRendererID.Index -- which nets ZERO, because the counter matches
`RendererID` in any spelling and the field is still named shaderRendererID.
The sort-key fix is the more consequential of the two (it stops sorting
identity-keyed draws by a driver name the command no longer carries), and the
proxy cannot see it at all. Do not read a flat counter as a flat slice.
PHASE 2 STEP 3, ITEM 4 (2026-08-02): the native-id TAIL. STEP 3 IS COMPLETE.
facade_native_id_params 67 -> 0; sweep_renderer_id 345 -> 168.
RendererAPI.h now declares no `u32 <name>ID` parameter at all. That is the
completion criterion, and it is the same kind of guarantee sweep_glad_includes
gives one level down: a translation unit in the sweep bucket that holds a
native name has nothing to pass it to, so the boundary is compiler-enforced
rather than measured.
THE PLAN SAID THIS COUNTER WOULD DRAIN PER ENTRY POINT. IT DID NOT, and the
reason generalises. Each u32 form was supposed to go as its last caller
migrated; in practice the last caller of nearly every form is another form's
caller (ResolveTexture feeds BindTexture, GetColorAttachmentRendererID feeds
CopyImageSubData, CreateTexture2D feeds SetTextureFilter), so the facade
flipped in one edit and ~250 call sites were then repaired against the
compiler's own (file, line) output. Budget a tail like this as ONE
indivisible change, not a drain.
QUERIES BECAME IDENTITIES -- the design question this item carried. Two
reasons, one of them concrete: RHI::ResourceKind::Query already existed in the
registry, so leaving them on u32 kept that enumerator dead; and
OcclusionQueryPool hands a query issued in frame N to BeginConditionalRender
in frame N+1, so a Shutdown()+Initialize() in between frees the names and GL
may reissue one -- gating a draw on an unrelated occlusion result, which looks
like a plausible frame rather than a broken one. A retired handle resolves to
0 and the conditional render is skipped instead.
CreateQueries is where the .data() trap recorded above applies LITERALLY (that
warning was written about this function). The out-span never reaches the
driver: the backend creates into its own std::vector<GLuint>, registers each
name, and writes handles back. DeleteQueries resolves AND unregisters, with
the same wrong-kind guard the other Delete* virtuals carry.
IsQueryResultAvailable answers false for a stale handle rather than reading
query 0 -- for occlusion a zero result reads as 'fully occluded', so the
honest-looking answer is the one that deletes geometry.
TWO SILENT DEFECTS, both the same shape, neither a type error, both found by
reading rather than by a test:
1. DeclareTransientTexture(name, desc, backingTextureID) set ONLY the native
id. That call publishes ShadowMapCSM / ShadowMapAtlas / their compare-off
raw views into the frame graph, and every consumer reads them through
ResolveTextureHandle -- which answers null for an entry with no Handle. So
DeferredLightingPass would have fallen through to the CSM placeholder every
frame: shadows gone, no error, no failing assertion.
2. The transient planner's ALIAS FAN-OUT set only the native id. Pass 1
(WillAllocate) sets both since slice 7; pass 2 -- the entries that inherit a
sibling's physical resource under aliasing -- still set TextureID alone, so
the aliased half of any plan resolved to a null identity. Worse than (1)
because it is load-dependent: it appears only when the planner decides to
alias, which depends on the frame's resource lifetimes.
THE RULE, and it corrects PhysicalTexture's own comment: 'TextureID and Handle
are ALTERNATIVES, exactly one is set' is right for an IMPORT, where the
importer holds one currency and neither is derivable from the other. It is
wrong everywhere THE GRAPH ITSELF does the setting, because there it holds the
resource object and reads both off one pointer in one statement. Slice 7
learned this for the transient acquire and fixed that site; item 4 found two
more governed by the same rule. Next time, grep EVERY assignment to .TextureID
and check each for a matching .Handle, rather than fixing the one the current
slice happens to touch.
TWO WORKLIST 'BLOCKERS' WERE PHANTOMS, in opposite directions:
* VertexBuffer / IndexBuffer 'expose no GetRHIHandle()' -- true and
irrelevant. Their accessor is spelled GetBufferHandle() and is used only
inside Platform/OpenGL/; what the consumers actually hold is a
Ref<StorageBuffer>, which has minted handles since slice 2. The gap was
recorded by reasoning about the type family instead of grepping the
accessor the caller uses.
* 'An import may only move to ImportTextureHandle after the diagnostics can
read one' -- still true, and already satisfied. #736's
Debug::NativeTextureIdForDiagnostics unblocked six imports at once (DDGI's
atlases, the colour-grading LUT, the fluid intermediates, the fog volumes,
the TAA/clouds history, the virtual-geometry debug target). A sequencing
constraint that has been MET reads exactly like one still blocking.
THE IBL TRIO'S SECOND CURRENCY DIED WITH ITS ONLY REASON TO EXIST. SetGlobalIBL
took four identities AND three native ids; the natives existed for exactly
three lines of RenderPipeline's graph.ImportTexture(...), because at the time
the graph could not import an identity. Switching those to ImportTextureHandle
removed the parameters, three Renderer3DData fields, three accessors, and the
'both currencies clear together' comment that existed to keep them in step.
When a value carries two currencies, find the single consumer that forced it.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. GetRendererID() still exists on the resource
classes -- it is what Platform/ and Renderer/Debug/ are supposed to use, and
the graph's diagnostics path reads it on purpose. Item 4 removes every way for
the SWEEP BUCKET to use one, not the accessor; deleting that is Phase 8, with
the tools relocation. The creators keep their ...Handle suffix (slice 4 called
it temporary; renaming ~40 call sites buys nothing and Phase 3 reshapes the
create family anyway). shaderRendererID keeps its FIELD NAME on the POD command
structs -- it has been an RHI::ResourceHandle since slice 6, and those 114
mentions are the bulk of the remaining 168.
PHASE 3 CONVERSION (2026-08-03): 232 -> 208. Eleven shaders and 24 sites are
converted (SSAO, AOApply, FXAA, ChromaticAberration, ColorGrading,
MotionBlur, TAA, ContactShadow, DOF, EASU, Fog). The remainder splits into
~128 mechanical pass binds, ~21 material-path sites behind the redundant-bind
cache, and 38 BindImageTexture (storage-image) sites the sampler-only heap
does not model at all -- see ADR 0011 amendment (26). Keep the docs and this
number in step: three passages quoted mid-conversion figures on the first
push and CodeRabbit caught the drift.
PHASE 3 (2026-08-02): THE BINDLESS REHEARSAL. A fourth counter,
sweep_bind_texture_sites, and it is the first one here whose target is NOT
zero. Read that difference before reading the number.
sweep_bind_texture_sites = occurrences of `BindTexture(` or
`BindImageTexture(` outside Platform/ and
Renderer/Debug/, counted after comments and
string literals are blanked. Under heap-bindless
a pass writes RHI::OffsetOf(view) into a UBO and
the shader indexes the heap, so every one of
these is a site the model deletes (ADR 0011
section 1.3 item 1).
WHY ZERO IS NOT THE TARGET, and why that is a design decision rather than a
shortfall. ARB_bindless_texture is not universally available, so the
slot-based path has to survive as the fallback on any device without it. A
zero here would mean the engine had stopped working on those machines. The
counter is therefore a MONOTONE-DOWN progress measure with a floor guard
(> 20) rather than a completion criterion -- the opposite shape from
facade_native_id_params, which was a completion criterion precisely because
the type system could enforce it. There is no type-system equivalent here:
both paths must compile, so nothing can make the old one unrepresentable.
THE FINDING THAT RESHAPED THE PHASE, and it is a toolchain constraint rather
than a design one. Every production shader travels
GLSL -> shaderc(target=vulkan 1.2) -> SPIR-V -> SPIRV-Cross -> GLSL 450
-> shaderc(target=opengl 4.5) -> OpenGL SPIR-V -> glSpecializeShader.
GL_ARB_bindless_texture is a GLSL-only extension that predates SPIR-V and has
no representation in the Vulkan target environment, so bindless GLSL cannot
enter that pipeline at all. Pinned by BindlessShaderPipelineTest, which
compiles a real bindless shader with the real target environments and fails
if the answer ever changes -- including if it changes to YES, because that
would make a whole compile route deletable.
The consequence is the sharpest thing this rehearsal produced for Phase 4:
the SHADER-SIDE mechanism does not transfer, and neither does most of the
backend (residency, texture immutability, sampler folding are all
ARB_bindless_texture-specific and have no VK_EXT_descriptor_heap analogue).
What DOES transfer is everything above the backend interface -- views owning
slots, the two lifetime classes, offsets as data, fetch-don't-store, poison
on free -- which is exactly the part ADR 0011 designed and exactly the part
that was worth rehearsing somewhere debuggable.
ONE HAZARD THE PREVIOUS PHASE'S DESIGN CREATES, found by building on it.
ResourceRegistry deliberately PRESERVES a handle across an in-place reload
(ScopedResourceHandle::Sync repoints, never retires) -- that is what makes
caching a ResourceHandle safe. A descriptor does not inherit that safety: an
ARB_bindless_texture handle names the underlying object, so recreated storage
leaves every descriptor naming a deleted object while the view's own
generation is unchanged, and OffsetOf cannot detect it. This is the exact
mirror image of the slice-6 finding, where stable identity made the
redundant-bind cache SKIP a bind that had to happen. Same root cause,
opposite symptom, same remedy: every site that recreates a resource's storage
must call RHI::DescriptorHeap::InvalidateResource, exactly as it must call
InvalidateTextureBinding.
PHASE 3, BUCKET 3 (2026-08-03): STORAGE IMAGES. 208 -> 178.
Every one of the 30 removed sites is a BindImageTexture: that family goes
36 -> 6, and the 6 are the honest floor rather than remaining work. They
are, exhaustively:
* RendererAPI.h (1) and RenderCommand.h (2) -- the pure-virtual
DECLARATION and the facade's declaration + forward. Nothing to convert;
the counter matches a declaration the same way it matches a call.
* HeapBindingSeam.cpp (1) -- BindImageOrOffset's OWN fallback call. This
is the degradation path and it is permanent: ARB_bindless_texture is not
universally available, so a machine without it must still bind. Deleting
this would delete the fallback, not the coupling.
* VirtualGeometryPass.cpp (2) -- deliberately NOT converted, and the
reason is worth more than the two counts. They feed
VirtualMeshGBuffer.glsl, and the bindless compile route produces no
SPIR-V and so never runs Reflect(), which leaves m_IsDeferredCapable
false and misroutes a G-Buffer shader into the forward-overlay fallback
(OpenGLShader::CreateProgramFromRawGLSL detects and errors on exactly
this). Converting the CALL SITES alone would have been safe -- the seam
forks on Shader::IsBoundProgramBindless(), so an unconverted program
still gets a real bind -- and would have bought two counter points and
nothing else. That is the shape of change this counter exists to
discourage, so they stay and say why in place.
WHAT THE 30 COST, and it is NOT what 'more call sites' implies. Amendment
(26) predicted a second heap-side feature before a second sweep, and that
held exactly. The call-site edits were the small half:
* A SECOND DESCRIPTOR KIND. RHI::ViewUsage {Sampled, Storage} on ViewDesc,
plus StorageAccess; glGetImageHandleARB in the backend with its own
residency namespace. IDescriptorHeapBackend grew a `usage` parameter on
ReleaseDescriptor and NullDescriptor, because GL's two residency
namespaces have two entry-point pairs and the spec does not promise a
texture handle and an image handle are numerically distinguishable -- a
u64 alone cannot say which call to make.
* A SECOND RESERVED NULL SLOT (kNullStorageHeapOffset = 1). A null is per
DESCRIPTOR KIND, not per heap: `image2D(samplerHandle)` is undefined in
exactly the way `image2D(0)` is, so pointing a cleared image binding at
slot 0 would have swapped a stale-read bug for an undefined-behaviour
one. This generalises the 'unbind has no translation' finding: enumerate
the KINDS that need a null, not just the operations.
* A DISJOINT INDEX REGION in the offset table (HEAP_IMAGE_SLOT_BASE = 64,
table grown to uvec4[18]). GL image units and texture units are separate
namespaces that both start at zero, so image unit 0 and TEX_DIFFUSE
would have collided in a single-index table and each silently rendered
the other's resource.
* RESIDENCY WIDENING. glGetImageHandleARB takes no access, so a read-only
and a read-write view of the same (texture, level, layer, format) are
literally the same handle -- but reading a WRITE_ONLY-resident handle is
undefined and a second residency transition is an INVALID_OPERATION.
GTAO does exactly this within one frame (edge texture written by the
main pass, read by denoise), so the backend re-makes the handle resident
READ_WRITE and counts it.
THREE DEFECTS THIS BUCKET SURFACED, none of them a type error:
1. THE PERSISTENT MEMO CACHE COULD NOT TELL TWO VIEWS APART. Its key was
(resource, samplerSlot, depthCompare) -- sound only because the GL
backend declined every view that was not the whole resource, so no two
distinguishable views could reach it. HZBGenerator asks for FOUR MIPS of
one texture in one dispatch; under that key the second, third and fourth
would each have been served the first's view and the whole pyramid would
have been written at level 0 -- a plausible frame with a broken occlusion
pyramid. The key now carries the whole ViewDesc. GENERALISABLE: a cache
key that is 'sufficient' only because a downstream layer refuses the
distinguishing cases is a latent bug with a scheduled trigger date.
2. InvalidateResource PUBLISHED A ZERO DESCRIPTOR on a failed re-acquire.
The comment beside it said 'poisoning renders black, which is the honest
answer'; the code stored the returned 0. A zero bindless handle is not
black -- sampling one is UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR, which is the entire reason
NullDescriptor is a real resident texture rather than a constant. So the
failure path rested on driver luck, and it is reached precisely when
something has already gone wrong. Pre-existing; fixed here.
3. Shader::SetBoundProgramBindless WAS PUBLISHED BY GRAPHICS SHADERS ONLY.
OpenGLComputeShader::Bind() never touched it, so binding a bindless
graphics program and then a compute program left the flag TRUE -- and the
first converted compute pass would have recorded offsets into a table its
program never declares while binding nothing at all. Latent rather than
live (nothing in compute was converted yet), and it would have presented
as garbage in a compute output with no diagnostic anywhere. Both Bind()s
now publish and both Unbind()s retract.
ONE PLEASANT SURPRISE, recorded because it inverts the obvious estimate:
COMPUTE SHADERS NEEDED NO SECOND COMPILE ROUTE. Amendment (19) established
that bindless GLSL cannot enter the shaderc(vulkan) pipeline, and the
graphics side needed CreateProgramFromRawGLSL to work around it.
OpenGLComputeShader::Compile has ALWAYS handed include-resolved GLSL
straight to glShaderSource -- it never travelled that pipeline -- so all it
needed was the same #extension/#define prologue injection. Budgeting this
bucket from the graphics route's cost would have over-estimated it
substantially. Check whether the constraint you are routing around actually
applies to the subsystem you are about to convert.
AND ONE ERGONOMIC DIFFERENCE from the sampler path, which the recipe in
docs/agent-rules/glsl-shaders.md now documents: an image macro DECLARES
rather than expanding to an expression. The format qualifier belongs to a
declaration and an image initialised from a buffer read is not a constant
expression, so it cannot live at file scope -- the declaration moves into
the function that uses it (WriteMip() in HZB.comp, not main()). The BODY is
still byte-identical between the two variants, which is the property that
keeps a conversion reviewable.

ONLY HALF OF THIS BUCKET IS DONE, deliberately, and the other half is a
DIFFERENT MECHANISM rather than more call sites (ADR 0011 amendment (32)).
FlushOffsets() re-establishes the heap's SSBO binding. Per PASS that is free —
the table is written once and read by every draw in the pass. The MATERIAL
path changes textures per DRAW, so a converted material shader would need a
flush per draw, which gives back exactly the cost bindless exists to remove
('bound once per frame, never per draw'). Converting it that way would be a
measurable REGRESSION that this counter would record as a win.
So: every bind here is routed through the seam (correct, and inert while no
bindless material program is in flight, because the seam falls back), and the
material SHADERS are deliberately not converted. Skybox.glsl IS converted — it
draws once per frame, so it pays the flush once and proves the
command-dispatch path works end to end through the heap. The real second half
is baking per-material offsets into PODMaterialData, which ADR 0011 §1.2
already describes ('stable for the object's life, so it can be baked once into
material data') and which is a data-layout change, not a binding one.
TWO TRAPS THIS BUCKET SURFACED:
1. A REDUNDANT-BIND CACHE MUST NOT SHORT-CIRCUIT AN OFFSET WRITE.
BoundTextures[slot] means 'this slot's GL BINDING is already correct',
which is sound because a binding persists until something rebinds it and
every tracked rebind goes through one helper. It does NOT mean 'this slot's
OFFSET is already correct': the offset table is shared with every pass that
binds through the seam, and those passes do not touch this array. Skipping
the write would leave another pass's offset in the slot and sample a
different real texture — and it saves nothing, because the write is a CPU
array store rather than a driver call.
HeapBinding::WritesOffsetsForBoundProgram() exists for this distinction and
for nothing else.
2. THE FALLBACK HAS TO GO THROUGH THE CALLER'S RendererAPI&. The dispatch
handlers receive one by reference, and CommandDispatchTest /
FramePipelineTest execute packets against MockRendererAPI, which records
every BindTexture. Routing the fallback through the static RenderCommand
facade instead keeps compiling, keeps working in the editor, and silently
stops the mock ever seeing the call — the .data() trap of amendment (14) in
a new place: a redirection the type system cannot object to. The seam
therefore carries an api-taking overload whose ONLY job is the fallback.

WHY A PUBLISHED BINDING CANNOT USE THE ORDINARY SEAM. BindTextureOrOffset
forks on Shader::IsBoundProgramBindless(), i.e. on the program CURRENTLY in
flight. That is the right question for a pass binding its own inputs before
its own draw, and a meaningless one for a slot published for LATER passes:
at publish time the consumer is not bound and may not exist yet. Worse, a
published slot can have consumers of BOTH kinds — TEX_DDGI_IRRADIANCE is read
by the DDGI shaders and DeferredLighting (convertible) AND by Skybox_GBuffer,
which can never convert because the bindless route produces no SPIR-V and so
never runs Reflect(). With mixed consumers there is no correct branch.
PublishTextureOffsetAndBind therefore does BOTH: stages the offset and issues
the bind. A bindless consumer reads the offset, a slot-based one reads the
binding, neither can tell the other happened. The cost is one redundant bind
on a PER-PASS path, not per draw.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS COUNTER, and it is not a shortfall: a publish call still
contains a real bind, so it does NOT reduce the count the way a converted
pass-local site does. The ratchet will always move less than the raw site
count suggests once published state is involved. Do not chase the difference.

Particle_Billboard_GPU.glsl reads gl_InstanceIndex — the VULKAN spelling. The

naming a GL_KHR_vulkan_glsl builtin is unconvertible until the bindless route
gains a translation step (glsl-shaders.md §5c-bis).
